title: Complementarity, Augmentation, or Substitutivity? The Impact of Generative Artificial Intelligence on the U.S. Federal Workforce
abstract: arXiv:2503.09637v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: This study applies a multi-stage Retrieval-Augmented Generation system, which grounds large language model assessments in curated evidence, to evaluate generative AI's near-term impact on knowledge, skills, and abilities across several hundred federal occupational series. Each occupation is scored along three dimensions of complementarity (AI enhances existing competencies), augmentation (AI requires workers to transform competencies), and substitutivity (AI replaces human tasks). Results reveal that generative AI primarily complements and augments federal roles, with limited substitution potential. Even occupations scoring highest on substitutivity reflect partial automation of routine subtasks rather than position elimination. These findings caution against blunt workforce reductions premised on displacement and instead support targeted reskilling, competency-based planning, and human-AI collaboration. translated_title: 互补、增强还是替代？生成式人工智能对美国联邦劳动力的影响
translated_abstract: 本研究应用一个多阶段的检索增强生成系统，该系统将大语言模型的评估建立在经过筛选的证据之上，用以评估生成式人工智能对数百个联邦职业系列中知识、技能和能力的近期影响。每个职业沿三个维度进行评分：互补性（AI增强现有能力）、增强性（AI要求工作者转变能力）和替代性（AI取代人类任务）。结果表明，生成式AI对联邦职位主要起互补和增强作用，替代潜力有限。即使是替代性得分最高的职业，也仅反映常规子任务的部分自动化，而非整个职位的消除。这些发现警示不应基于“取代”假设而采取简单粗暴的裁员措施，而应支持有针对性的再技能培训、基于能力的规划以及人机协作。
tldr: 本研究利用检索增强生成系统评估生成式AI对美国联邦各职业的影响，发现AI主要起互补和增强作用而非替代作用，因此应采取针对性再培训和人机协作策略，而非大规模裁员。
en_tdlr: This study uses a multi-stage Retrieval-Augmented Generation system to assess generative AI's impact across hundreds of U.S. federal occupational series, finding that AI primarily complements and augments rather than substitutes federal roles, supporting targeted reskilling and human-AI collaboration over workforce reductions.
